findings.claim: Signed favorable-minus-comparison endpoint contrasts at the observed selection nodes are strongest and most reproducible for the short-range pair-distance shell densities: pair_kernel_1.5 (integrated z 0.562, q 1.5e-4, positive batch fraction 1.0), pair_kernel_2.5 (0.631, q 2.2e-5, 1.0) and pair_kernel_3.5 (0.540, q 9.8e-5, 1.0), with pair_kernel_5.0 weaker (0.319, q 3.7e-3) and pair_kernel_7.0 reversed (-0.485, q 1.5e-4, positive batch fraction 0.0). The same ordering appears in the raw and adjusted branch correlations (pair_kernel_1.5 r=0.085/0.101, pair_kernel_2.5 r=0.088/0.084, pair_kernel_7.0 r=-0.055/-0.050). These are selection-enrichment contrasts on a radial shell-density observable, not an absolute geometric descriptor and not an interaction energy.

Shape anisotropy carries a consistent signed contrast: shape_yy is negative and reproducible (integrated z -0.513, q 1.5e-5, positive batch fraction 0.0; raw correlation -0.103, adjusted -0.100), with shape_xx (-0.495, q 8.1e-4) and shape_yz (-0.212, q 0.035) also negative, while shape_xz is positive but not significant (0.185, q 0.219). The regional local_cyy enrichment_z is negative at every landmark (e.g. landmark_00 -0.575, landmark_07 -0.646, landmark_16 -0.672, landmark_19 -0.622), so the yy contrast is not confined to one region.

Landmark soft-minimum distances and shell occupancies show mixed signs across landmarks rather than one global direction: softmin is negative at landmark_00 (-0.481), landmark_04 (-0.351), landmark_06 (-0.364) and landmark_18 (-0.311), but positive at landmark_03 (0.360), landmark_05 (0.396), landmark_15 (0.369) and landmark_16 (0.224); occupancy5 is positive at landmark_00 (0.208), landmark_04 (0.300) and landmark_13 (0.191) and negative at landmark_02 (-0.323), landmark_05 (-0.344), landmark_15 (-0.357) and landmark_18 (-0.311). Any landmark rule must therefore be region-specific, and the softmin sign is not a shared quality axis.

Global centroid coordinates carry no usable signed contrast: integrated z is -0.111 (x), -0.243 (y) and -0.061 (z) with q 0.257, 0.014 and 0.481, and after branch adjustment the centroid effects are indistinguishable from zero (adjusted covariance p 0.946/0.777/0.849; adjusted correlation p 0.701/0.622/0.386). Centroid translation is not a supported coordinate direction in this evidence.

Joint-motion diagnostics are the most reproducible branch-level signals and are negative: joint_innovation_RMS_A (raw covariance p 2.3e-3, adjusted p 6.6e-4, same-sign batch fraction 0.857/0.929), joint_internal_RMS_A (p 3.7e-3 / 1.4e-3, same-sign 0.786/0.929) and joint_translation_RMS_A (p 0.017 / 9.9e-3). The corresponding raw and adjusted correlations are negative (innovation -0.142/-0.150, internal -0.130/-0.137, translation -0.067/-0.076). These are joint-motion summaries, not a claim that a specific internal coordinate causes affinity.

Within-selector joint diagnostics separate coherent joint patterns from isolated marginals: innovation_native_alignment (0.092, q 2.2e-9, positive batch fraction 1.0) and teacher_innovation_contrast_alignment (0.226, q 2.2e-9, 1.0) are positive, whereas observed_child_score_gain is negative (-0.036, q 1.8e-7, positive batch fraction 0.0). The teacher contrast is dominated by its internal fraction (0.787) rather than translation (0.132) or rotation (0.081), and atom participation is 0.384. These are descriptive within-selector associations with batch as the independent unit, not causal effects.

The supplied continuous contrast functions are observed-node linear interpolations over the complete observed window [0.0,0.49] with no extrapolation allowed, and they are not well described by a constant rule: landmark_00_soft_mass has first/last rate z of +9.27/-10.00 with 4 sign changes and 1 strong sign conflict, landmark_02_soft_mass +55.9/+5.1 with 7 sign changes, landmark_06_local_dy -27.4/-11.3 with 3 sign changes, and landmark_18_local_dy -35.8/-9.2 with 3 sign changes. The curve-fidelity audit shows large relative node RMSE (0.30-0.99) and many strong sign-conflict nodes (up to 15 for landmark_16_occupancy5), so a time-conditioned rule is only defensible where a validated fit or observed-node interpolation supports it.

Several local displacement and off-diagonal shape curves are dominated by sign changes and strong sign conflicts rather than a stable trend: landmark_00_local_dy has first/last rate z -72.4/+5.5 with 6 sign changes and 4 strong conflicts, landmark_00_local_cxy +64.8/-19.7 with 9 sign changes and 14 strong conflicts, landmark_01_local_cxy +66.2/-22.9 with 7 sign changes and 18 strong conflicts, and landmark_18_local_cxz +32.3/+28.4 with 11 sign changes and 18 strong conflicts. These curves should not be treated as monotone coordinate rules.

Parent-child increment contrasts disagree in sign with the population endpoint contrasts for several features: shape_xx increment rate z is -3.70 (p 5.1e-3) and shape_yy -3.85 (p 0.016) while the population endpoint contrasts are also negative, but shape_xz is +3.00 (p 0.025) against a positive population contrast, pair_kernel_2.5 is +3.96 (p 0.031) against +0.63, pair_kernel_7.0 is -3.14 (p 0.031) against -0.485, and landmark_00_softmin is -4.91 (p 6.2e-4) against -0.481. Increment and population contrasts are different estimands and their disagreement should affect direction priorities rather than being averaged.

Turnover accounting shows large positive residual rates for the same local shape features whose population rates are near zero or negative: landmark_00_local_cxx population rate z -0.058 with edge rate -4.34 and residual +4.29 (p 2.1e-3), landmark_00_local_cyy population +0.258 with edge -4.79 and residual +5.05 (p 1.5e-3), landmark_04_local_cxx population +1.08 with edge -4.60 and residual +5.67 (p 2.5e-5), landmark_07_local_cxx population +0.385 with edge -4.69 and residual +5.08 (p 1.1e-4), and landmark_16_local_cyy population +0.465 with edge -5.90 and residual +6.37 (p 1.2e-4). The residual is an accounting diagnostic that mixes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not a causal selection effect or an atom velocity.

Available descendant survival credit is weak and mostly not significant after joint multiple testing: landmark_00_soft_mass survival enrichment z is +0.365 (p 7.8e-4, q 0.120), landmark_07_soft_mass +0.220 (p 0.042, q 0.356), landmark_10_soft_mass +0.234 (p 0.017, q 0.302) and landmark_18_local_czz +0.217 (p 9.7e-3, q 0.302), while landmark_19_local_czz change-rate z is -1.58 (p 0.018, q 0.302). Because decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable, this recorded joint-head survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.

The independent statistical unit is the batch (14 batches), the observed window is [0.0,0.5] with score times 0.0-0.49, and the terminal metadata place the terminal score at 0.99 and terminal state at 1.0, outside the observed support. The information audit reports compressed-choice excess fixed RMS 0.081 A (CI 0.070-0.092), top4 teacher overlap 0.470 (CI 0.427-0.515) and chosen teacher score correlation 0.102 (CI 0.065-0.140), and it states these are not the full score-weighted reward or its FLOWR Jacobian. The lineage table records 349 nodes with fewer than 3 ancestors and 531 with fewer than 6, so ancestral coverage is incomplete and survivor bias is expected in descendant credit.

hypotheses.claim: Hypothesis: the reproducible favorable direction is a short-range pair-distance shell density (pair_kernel_1.5-3.5) rather than a centroid translation, with the long-range shell pair_kernel_7.0 as the opposing comparison. Observable: pair_kernel_a for a in {1.5,2.5,3.5,5.0,7.0}. Intended response: increase the short-shell densities and decrease the 7.0 A shell density. Target origin: the observed selection nodes over the complete observed window. Scale: pair distances of roughly 1.5-3.5 A versus 7.0 A. Discriminating failure: if the short-shell endpoint contrast is not reproduced in independent batches or if the 7.0 A sign flips, the direction is not supported. This remains a measurable contrast, not a physical interaction energy.

Hypothesis: the yy component of the shape tensor is a reproducible negative-contrast coordinate across regions. Observable: shape_yy and the regional local_cyy enrichment. Intended response: decrease shape_yy. Target origin: all 20 landmarks, with the strongest negative regional values at landmarks 07, 16 and 19. Scale: shape entries in A^2. Discriminating failure: a positive shape_yy endpoint contrast or a positive local_cyy enrichment at a majority of landmarks would weaken the direction. The shape tensor is a coordinate covariance summary, not an inferred chemical mechanism.

Hypothesis: landmark soft-minimum distance and shell occupancy act in opposite directions at different landmarks, so a single global landmark rule is not supported. Observable: landmark_r_softmin and landmark_r_occupancy3/occupancy5. Intended response: decrease softmin at landmarks 00, 04, 06 and 18 while increasing it at landmarks 03, 05, 15 and 16. Target origin: the observed selection nodes. Scale: distances in A with softmin temperature 0.5 A and shell widths sigma 1.0 A. Discriminating failure: if the per-landmark signs are not stable across independent batches, the region-specific rule is not supported. Occupancy is a radial shell density, not an atom count.

Hypothesis: a time-conditioned contrast rule is preferable to a constant rule for the soft-mass and local-displacement curves that show large first-to-last rate changes and multiple sign changes. Observable: the supplied observed-node linear contrast functions over [0.0,0.49]. Intended response: follow the observed-node sign within the window rather than a fixed sign. Target origin: the shared observed score times. Scale: the full observed window, with no extrapolation beyond 0.49. Discriminating failure: if a validated fit or observed-node interpolation does not reproduce the sign changes, the time-conditioned rule is not supported. A contrast curve is not an absolute reward target.

Hypothesis: the disagreement between population contrasts and parent-child increment contrasts for shape_xz, pair_kernel_2.5, pair_kernel_7.0 and landmark_00_softmin reflects changing cohort composition and reclassification rather than within-path change, because the corresponding turnover residuals are large and positive. Observable: increment rate z and turnover residual rate for the same features. Intended response: treat increment and population contrasts as separate estimands and let their disagreement lower the priority of the affected features. Target origin: parent-child edges over the observed window. Scale: whole-window rates. Discriminating failure: if the residual is small relative to the edge rate, within-path change is the better explanation. The residual is an accounting diagnostic, not a causal selection effect.

Hypothesis: coherent joint-motion alignment, not isolated marginal descriptors, carries the reproducible signal, since innovation_native_alignment and teacher_innovation_contrast_alignment are positive with positive batch fraction 1.0 while observed_child_score_gain is negative, and the joint internal and innovation RMS contrasts are the most reproducible branch-level effects. Observable: joint_innovation_RMS_A, joint_internal_RMS_A and the alignment diagnostics. Intended response: reduce joint internal and innovation RMS while preserving native alignment. Target origin: the observed selection nodes. Scale: RMS in A. Discriminating failure: if the joint RMS contrasts lose their negative sign under branch adjustment or if alignment does not remain positive, the joint-motion hypothesis is not supported. These are joint-motion summaries, not a causal mechanism.

limitations: Descendant credit is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity; decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable.
Turnover residual includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not only resampling.
Adjusted branch covariance is supplied evidence; region moments themselves are not rigid-motion residuals.
Curve fitting does not establish causal benefit or a gradient; no time bins or outside-window analysis.
Static teachers are last-learning-node forecasts, not actual final structures.
All weak and null scalar effects retained; current study outcomes are withheld from design roles.
The information audit metrics are not the full score-weighted reward or its FLOWR Jacobian.
Ancestral coverage is incomplete (349 nodes with fewer than 3 ancestors, 531 with fewer than 6), so survivor bias is expected in descendant credit.
